title: Career hub cities in Asia with Ledger, part 7
summary: Part 7 of the career cities series covers 8 career hubs, one sourced fact each; rebuilt 18 Nov 2026 with Hoang's notes (plain title, new creative industries, logos with names in the city scene, paper and flat versions)
changesFromV1: Title is now plain and direct (Hoang, 18 Nov): 'Career hub cities in Asia with Ledger, part seven.' with a PART 7 pill
New creative stops (Hoang, 18 Nov): Bangkok for film and Singapore for video games (Sea's Garena)

Dropped to stay under 2:00: Seria and Kuala Lumpur (lead's first picks); Singapore moved from shipping to video games (shipping was already in Part 5 with Piraeus); Jakarta cosmetics and Manila animation were researched but had weaker sources
Voice lines shortened; Rayong now shows Changan, BYD and Great Wall Motor (all with plants in Rayong); logos with names in the city scene; the fact number counts up

beats.label: title
beats.voice: Career hub cities in Asia with Ledger, part seven.

beats.label: stop 1 Bac Ninh
beats.voice: First, Ledger lands in Bac Ninh, Vietnam, a hub for phones.

beats.label: stop 1 Bac Ninh
beats.voice: Samsung's plants here and nearby have made 2 billion phones.

beats.label: stop 2 Phnom Penh
beats.voice: Then, he flies to Phnom Penh, Cambodia, a hub for garments.

beats.label: stop 2 Phnom Penh
beats.voice: Cambodia's garment, shoe and travel goods factories employ over 900,000 people.

beats.label: stop 3 Bangkok
beats.voice: Next, he hops to Bangkok, Thailand, a hub for film.

beats.label: stop 3 Bangkok
beats.voice: In 2025, Thailand hosted 546 foreign film productions.

beats.label: stop 4 Rayong
beats.voice: Then, he rides to Rayong, Thailand, a hub for cars.

beats.label: stop 4 Rayong
beats.voice: Changan opened a plant here in 2025 for 10 billion baht.

beats.label: stop 5 Penang
beats.voice: Next, he flies to Penang, Malaysia, a hub for chips.

beats.label: stop 5 Penang
beats.voice: Intel's site here, opened in 1972, employs 15,000 people.

beats.label: stop 6 Singapore
beats.voice: Then, he flies to Singapore, a hub for video games.

beats.label: stop 6 Singapore
beats.voice: Sea, based here, drew over 100 million Garena players a day.

beats.label: stop 7 Morowali
beats.voice: Next, he hops to Morowali, Indonesia, a hub for nickel.

beats.label: stop 7 Morowali
beats.voice: Its industrial park had about 85,000 workers in 2024.

beats.label: stop 8 Manila
beats.voice: Finally, he lands in Manila, the Philippines, a hub for outsourced services.

beats.label: stop 8 Manila
beats.voice: The country's outsourcing industry employed 1.9 million people in 2025.

beats.label: summary
beats.voice: So that was Southeast Asia, from Bac Ninh to Manila.

beats.label: summary
beats.voice: Next, part eight maps South Asia, the Gulf and Central Asia.

beats.label: cta
beats.voice: To climb in these cities, you need a good business foundation.

beats.label: cta
beats.voice: Go to Edlintics.com to learn technical business skills.

stops.fact: Samsung's phone plants in Bac Ninh and Thai Nguyen had made 2 billion phones by the end of June 2025, with about 90,000 Vietnamese workers (plants, not a head office)
stops.source: Vietnam Government News, Samsung produces 2 billionth mobile phone in Viet Nam: https://en.baochinhphu.vn/samsung-produces-2-billionth-mobile-phone-in-viet-nam-1112508271304324.htm

stops.fact: Cambodia's garment, footwear and travel goods sector employs over 900,000 workers in more than 1,500 factories; its exports were US$15.5 billion in 2025 (a country figure; Phnom Penh is the capital)

Thailand hosted 546 foreign film productions in 2025, spending over 7.717 billion baht (Department of Tourism); Bangkok is among the most in-demand filming locations; GDH 559's head office is on Sukhumvit 31, Watthana, Bangkok
stops.source: The Nation, 14 Jan 2026: https://www.nationthailand.com/news/tourism/40061194 ; Government Public Relations Department, 21 Jul 2025: https://thailand.prd.go.th/en/content/category/detail/id/52/iid/407372 ; GDH 559 contact page: https://www.gdh559.com/contact

stops.fact: Changan Automobile began production at its first overseas plant, in Rayong, on 16 May 2025, an investment of about THB 10 billion with a capacity of 100,000 vehicles a year (a plant; the head office is in China); BYD (WHA Industrial Estate, Rayong) and Great Wall Motor (Pluak Daeng, Rayong) also have car plants in Rayong
stops.source: Gasgoo, 16 May 2025: https://autonews.gasgoo.com/articles/market-industry/changan-automobile-begins-production-at-rayong-plant-in-thailand-70037455 ; BYD plant: The Thaiger, BYD opens first EV plant in Thailand ; GWM Rayong plant: https://www.gwm-global.com/news/3401476.html

stops.fact: Intel's Penang site, opened in 1972, has a workforce of 15,000; Micron opened its second assembly and test site in Penang in 2023; Penang holds about 13% of global chip packaging (sites, not head offices)
Sea Limited (address 1 Fusionopolis Place, Galaxis, Singapore) says its games arm Garena connected on average with more than 100 million players daily throughout 2025
stops.source: Sea Limited, fourth quarter and full year 2025 results, Singapore, 3 Mar 2026 (cdn.sea.com results PDF) ; Sea contact page: https://www.sea.com/contact

stops.fact: The Indonesia Morowali Industrial Park (IMIP) had about 85,000 workers at the end of 2024; Indonesia produced nearly half of the world's nickel in 2022; Tsingshan owns a nickel smelter inside the park (a plant)
The Philippine IT and business process management industry employed 1.9 million people in 2025 and earned over USD 40 billion in export revenue (a country figure; Metro Manila is its main hub)

caption:
Career hub cities in Asia with Ledger, Part 7, goes to Southeast Asia with eight stops, and each stop shows one industry that city is a hub for, with a sourced fact

So you will meet Bac Ninh for phones, Phnom Penh for garments, Bangkok for film, Rayong for cars, Penang for chips, Singapore for video games, Morowali for nickel, and Manila for outsourced services

Save the map for later, because Part 8 maps career hub cities across South Asia, the Gulf and Central Asia
